We need to return all possible precursors of applying the template (from previous step) to the molecule. We have template_id 1914384 and mapped_rxn given. The initial molecule is the product? The mapped_rxn shows forward reaction: left side is reactants? Actually mapped_rxn: '([CH3:1]/[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)=[CH:9]/[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C:13](=[O:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18])>>([CH3:1][C@H:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)[C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18])'

So forward reaction: reactant (with double bond etc) -> product (with saturated ring and OH). The initial_molecule is the product (the right side). So we need to apply retrosynthetic template (reverse of forward) to product to get precursors (reactants). Use apply_template tool with molecule_smiles = product SMILES (but we have atom-mapped SMILES). Need to convert to normal SMILES? The product SMILES given includes atom mapping and stereochemistry: [CH3:1][C@H:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)[C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]

We can feed that directly to apply_template? The tool expects SMILES string of target molecule (no mapping). Might accept mapping? Probably not. We could strip mapping numbers and brackets? But easier: use apply_template with the template_id and the product SMILES (maybe without mapping). That's a cyclobutane? Actually 5-member? Let's just use the given string as is; tool may handle mapping? Not sure.
